items.prompt: The data folder is empty. The user adds the very first book. What does the app print?
items.answer: "Book added with ID 0." since the highest-id search starts at -1
distractors: "Book added with ID 1." since every id counter is started at one
"Book added with ID 1." since the list size plus one is used
"Book added." with no ID until the data is first saved
items.explanation: findNextBookId starts with highestId = -1 and returns highestId + 1; with no books that is 0, and addBook uses nextBookId++ (reproduced: "Book added with ID 0."). Nothing uses the list size, and the id is assigned in memory before any save.

items.prompt: Ann (borrower ID 0) already has one book checked out. She now checks out a second, available book. What happens?
items.answer: It succeeds, as no rule limits how many books one borrower holds
distractors: It is refused, with a message saying that she already has a book out
It is refused until the first book has been returned by Ann herself
It succeeds only if none of the books she holds is overdue
items.explanation: checkOutBook checks three things: the book exists, the borrower exists, and that book is not already checked out. Nothing counts a borrower's current loans or looks at their due dates, so the second checkout succeeds.

items.prompt: Book 0 is already checked out. A user tries to check it out again, typing borrower ID 9, which does not exist. What does the app print?
items.answer: "Borrower not found." as the borrower check comes before the checked-out check
distractors: "Book is already checked out." as that check runs before the borrower lookup
"Book not found." since a book that is out is skipped by findBookById
Both messages, "Borrower not found." and then "Book is already checked out."
items.explanation: checkOutBook returns at the first failed check, in the order book exists, borrower exists, book not checked out. Book 0 exists, borrower 9 does not, so it returns "Borrower not found." (reproduced). findBookById searches every book regardless of state, and each check returns, so only one message is possible.

items.prompt: At checkout the user enters the due date 2000-01-01. What happens?
items.answer: It is accepted, and the next listing marks the book (OVERDUE)
distractors: It is refused, and the app asks again for a date in the future
It is refused with "Please use the YYYY-MM-DD format." again
It is accepted, but OVERDUE only shows from the next day on
items.explanation: readOptionalDate only checks that LocalDate.parse accepts the text, and checkOutBook stores the date it is given. isOverdue compares the due date with today, and 2000-01-01 is before today, so the very next list shows (OVERDUE) (reproduced; the checklist records it too).

items.prompt: A book is checked out and its due date is today's date. How does option 2 show its status?
items.answer: Checked out with its due date shown and no (OVERDUE) mark after it
distractors: Checked out, and (OVERDUE) is added as the date is not in the future
Overdue, since a book that is due today counts as late from midnight
Available, since a due date of today ends the loan on its own
items.explanation: isOverdue is checkedOut && dueDate != null && dueDate.isBefore(today). isBefore is strict, so a date equal to today is not before it and no mark is added (reproduced with today's date). Nothing ever returns a book automatically.

items.prompt: At checkout the user just presses Enter at the optional due date prompt. What is stored for the loan?
items.answer: A loan with no due date, which isOverdue can then never flag
distractors: A due date 14 days after today, which is the default loan length
A due date equal to the checkout date, so it is overdue tomorrow
Nothing, as the checkout is cancelled when the due date is blank
items.explanation: readOptionalDate returns null for blank input, checkOut stores it as is, and saveBooks writes dueDate= with an empty value. isOverdue requires dueDate != null, so this loan is never reported overdue. There is no default loan length anywhere in the code.

items.prompt: The user adds a book and then the input ends (Ctrl+D, or a piped script runs out) before option 8 or 9. Is the new book in books.txt?
items.answer: No; the exception ends the program and nothing saved it
distractors: Yes; addBook writes books.txt straight after adding
Yes; a finally block in run() saves the data on every exit
Yes; LibraryManager saves whenever its lists change
items.explanation: run() has no try/finally: the NoSuchElementException from scanner.nextLine escapes and ends the program. Data only reaches disk through saveData, which options 8 and 9 call (reproduced: the title was not in books.txt). The README says so too.

items.prompt: Someone hand-edits books.txt so a book has dueDate=15-10-2026. What happens at the next start?
items.answer: It crashes with an uncaught DateTimeParseException and a stack trace
distractors: It prints "Could not load library data:" and the reason, then exits
That book loads with no due date, and all the other books load
That book is skipped with a warning, and the others still load
items.explanation: parseDateOrNull calls LocalDate.parse, which throws DateTimeParseException, a runtime exception. main only catches IOException, so the friendly message is never printed and the JVM prints a stack trace (reproduced). Nothing skips or repairs a bad record.

items.prompt: A record in books.txt has title= and author= lines but no id= line, and another book already has ID 0. What happens on load?
items.answer: It loads as a second book with ID 0, beside the first one
distractors: Startup fails with a NumberFormatException for the id
The record is skipped, as id is a required field in every record
It gets the next free id, one above the highest id loaded so far
items.explanation: loadBooks reads the id with record.getOrDefault("id", "0"), so a missing id becomes 0 and parses fine. No uniqueness check exists, so two books share ID 0 (reproduced: both listed as ID 0). The checklist notes this can silently duplicate an id.

items.prompt: A checked-out book's borrowerId names a borrower who is not in borrowers.txt. What status does option 2 show for that book?
items.answer: Checked out on its date, with the due date, but no borrower name
distractors: Available, since a loan whose borrower is gone is dropped on load
Checked out to Unknown, on its date, followed by the due date
None; startup stops because the borrower link fails to resolve
items.explanation: buildBookStatus starts "Checked out" and appends " to <name>" only inside borrower.ifPresent(...); findBorrowerForBook returns Optional.empty() when no borrower has that id. The dates are still appended (reproduced with an empty borrowers.txt). Loading never cross-checks the two files.

items.prompt: A checked-out book is returned and the data is saved. What does its record in books.txt now hold?
items.answer: checkedOut=false, with borrowerId, checkedOutAt and dueDate blank
distractors: checkedOut=false, and the last borrowerId is kept as loan history
Nothing; a returned book is left out until it is loaned again
checkedOut=false, with the old due date kept for the next loan
items.explanation: Book.returnBook sets checkedOut to false and the borrower id and both dates to null; saveBooks writes null as an empty value through valueOrBlank (reproduced). Every book is written whatever its state, and no history is kept.

items.prompt: The app starts in a folder with no data directory, and the user chooses 9 at once. What exists on disk afterwards?
items.answer: A data folder holding an empty books.txt and an empty borrowers.txt
distractors: Nothing new, since there were no books and no borrowers to be saved
Only the data folder; each file appears after its first record
Nothing; startup fails because data/books.txt cannot be found
items.explanation: load() calls Files.createDirectories and treats missing files as empty lists. Option 9 calls saveData, and save() writes both files with Files.write even when the line lists are empty (reproduced: both files exist and are 0 bytes).

items.front: Why does a Book store a borrowerId instead of a Borrower object?
items.back: It keeps the model simple and the files flat: books.txt stores one number per loan, and LibraryManager looks the borrower up by id when it is needed (findBorrowerForBook). The cost is that nothing guarantees the id still points at a saved borrower.

items.front: What does FileStorage.clean protect against when saving?
items.back: It replaces each line-feed (newline) character with a space, and null with an empty string, so every saved value stays on one key=value line. Otherwise the text after a newline would land on a line of its own, and readRecords would read it as a separate key instead of part of the title. A lone carriage return is not replaced.

items.front: Why does Book have two constructors?
items.back: One builds a new, available book from title, author and ISBN. The other rebuilds a book from saved data, including its checkout state, borrower id and dates, so loading can restore a loan exactly as it was saved.
